issues.title: Test function missing REDIS_TEST wrapper
issues.description: The rule requires that all test functions and test-specific code in source files must be enclosed within #ifdef REDIS_TEST / #endif blocks, but the validateStoredKeyConversion function is a test/validation function that exists without the required preprocessor wrapper
issues.rule_name: Test Functions Must Be Wrapped in REDIS_TEST Preprocessor Blocks

issues.title: Stored-key used for lookup instead of extracted key in defragmentation
issues.description: In activeDefragHfieldAndUpdateRef, the code extracts the lookup key from the stored-key (Entry*) using dictStoredKey2Key but then passes the original stored-key pointer to dictFindLink. After the API refactoring, dictFindLink expects a lookup key, not a stored-key. This will cause hash mismatches and comparison failures, leading to dictFindLink returning NULL when it should find the entry. The serverAssert on the next line will then trigger, crashing the server during active defragmentation of hash fields.

issues.title: Wrong stored-key pointer used for dict lookup after keyDup
issues.description: In dictSetKeyAtLink when newItem is 0 and *link is NULL, the function attempts to find the link by calling dictFindLink with addedKey. However, addedKey is the result of keyDup (if keyDup is configured) or the original stored-key, and dictFindLink expects a lookup key. Additionally, after keyDup, addedKey may point to a newly allocated object with a different address than the original key in the dict, causing the lookup to fail even with pointer comparison. This will cause the assertion to fail, or worse, result in corrupted dict state if the assertion is disabled.

issues.title: Unused local variable triggers -Werror build failure
issues.description: A new local variable `key` is introduced but never used. This will typically produce an `-Wunused-variable` warning, which becomes a build error under `-Werror`, violating the requirement that the build compiles cleanly with warnings treated as errors.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
const void *key = dictStoredKey2Key(d, ptr);
    link = dictFindLink(d, ptr, NULL);
issues.rule_name: Rule 4: Build Must Compile Without Warnings When -Werror is Enabled

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14646 - Replace fragile dict stored-key API with getKeyId callback
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes the global `dictUseStoredKeyApi()` flag and the `storedHashFunction`/`storedKeyCompare` callbacks from dict. In their place it adds one `dictType.keyFromStoredKey` callback and a private `dictStoredKey2Key()` helper. Every dict entry point that walks a chain now converts the stored object to a lookup key itself. Callers in `kvstore.c`, `rdb.c`, `t_hash.c`, `module.c` and `defrag.c` lose their set/reset bracketing, and `hashTypeDelete()` drops its `isSdsField` argument. I grepped `src`, `tests` and `modules` at the head commit and found no remaining references to the removed APIs. The hash-field dict types have no conversion callback, which is safe because an `Entry*` is the field sds (`entryGetField()` in `src/entry.h`), so their stored key and lookup key are the same pointer. The db dicts use `kvGetKey` in `src/server.c`.

The core refactor is sound and removes a fragile global-state toggle. I did not find a bug that is reachable on today's call paths. However, two spots in the diff are wrong or misleading. In `dictSetKeyAtLink()` the `newItem == 0` branch now passes `addedKey` (a stored object, possibly a duplicate of one) to the lookup-key API `dictFindLink()`. In `activeDefragHfieldAndUpdateRef()` a converted `key` is computed and never used. Both happen to work today only because of the Entry-equals-sds identity. The diff also adds an unused static helper and some unrelated churn, and it adds no tests.
structured_output.verdictRationale: No currently reachable bug was confirmed. The db-dict `newItem == 0` path in `db.c` always passes a non-NULL link, and hash dicts have an identity conversion. But the PR touches exactly these lines to fix the stored-vs-lookup distinction and gets two of them wrong. Those are cheap to fix before merge. The unused helper and unused variable also add compiler warnings under the project's `-Wall`.

architecture.overview:
Redis dict is a chained hash table, and the `dictType` describes how keys are hashed and compared. Before this PR, dicts whose stored element (a `kvobj` in the keyspace, or an `Entry*` for hash fields) differs from the lookup key (an sds) needed a global toggle, `dictUseStoredKeyApi()`, set around each operation. The toggle also selected `storedHashFunction` and `storedKeyCompare` callbacks. Callers had to bracket every call correctly, and missing one was an easy bug to introduce.

After this PR, each dict type declares a single `keyFromStoredKey` callback. `dictStoredKey2Key()` in `dict.c` applies it wherever the dict walks a chain or inserts. The db dicts (`dbDictType`, `dbExpiresDictType` in `server.c`) use `kvGetKey`, which returns the sds inside the `kvobj`. Hash-field dicts keep no callback because the `Entry*` is itself the field sds. Lookup-key callers such as `dictFind` are unchanged, and the bracketing at call sites in `kvstore.c`, `rdb.c`, `t_hash.c` and `module.c` is removed.
steps: Entry point: callers in `src/db.c` and `src/kvstore.c` (`kvstoreDictAddRaw`, `kvstoreDictSetAtLink`) pass a stored `kvobj` into the dict, and `src/t_hash.c` passes sds field names for hash operations.

Dict internals in `src/dict.c`: `dictAddRaw`, `dictGenericDelete`, `dictFindLinkInternal`, `dictFindLinkForInsert` and `dictTwoPhaseUnlinkFind` now each call `dictStoredKey2Key()` on the chain node, or on their input in the insert path, before hashing or comparing. `dictGetHash()` always uses `hashFunction`.
Type contract in `src/dict.h`: `keyFromStoredKey` is the only new callback. The `__stored_key` annotation is documentation only and expands to nothing.
Concrete wiring in `src/server.c`: `kvGetKey` replaces `dictHashKV` and `dictCompareKV` for db dicts. `dictSdsCompareKV` now compares two sds values and no longer reads a kvobj.

Behavioural checks worth a reviewer's attention: `dictSetKeyAtLink(newItem=0)` in `src/dict.c` and the defrag path in `src/defrag.c` (`activeDefragHfieldAndUpdateRef`) still pass stored objects to lookup-key functions. They are correct only through the identity conversion.

findings.title: dictSetKeyAtLink newItem=0 passes a stored object to a lookup-key API
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/dict.c`, function `dictSetKeyAtLink` (around lines 911-916), the `newItem == 0` branch calls `dictFindLink(d, addedKey, NULL)` when `*link` is NULL. `addedKey` is a stored object or a keyDup copy, but `dictFindLink` expects a lookup key. Change the call to convert the original `key` with `dictStoredKey2Key(d, key)`, matching the `newItem == 1` branch a few lines above. Keep `addedKey` for the insertion itself. Do not change behaviour for dicts without `keyFromStoredKey`.

findings.title: Converted key computed but unused in defrag, and stored key still passed to dictFindLink
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/defrag.c`, function `activeDefragHfieldAndUpdateRef` (around lines 278-284), the new `const void *key = dictStoredKey2Key(d, ptr);` is never used, and `dictFindLink(d, ptr, NULL)` still gets the stored `ptr`. Make the lookup use the converted key, `dictFindLink(d, key, NULL)`, so the variable is actually used. Alternatively, remove the unused conversion and add a one-line comment that hash-field dicts use the `Entry*` as its own lookup key. Keep the `dictSetKeyAtLink` call and the `serverAssert(link)` unchanged.

findings.title: validateStoredKeyConversion is an unused static function
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/dict.c`, delete the unused `static int validateStoredKeyConversion(...)` helper (around lines 101-109). Nothing calls it, and it triggers `-Wunused-function` under `-Wall`. If a runtime check is wanted, add it as a `debugAssert` at the call sites of `dictStoredKey2Key` rather than as a standalone helper.

findings.title: No tests added for the reworked stored-key paths
findings.body:
The diff changes the key conversion in every dict chain walk, the `dictSetKeyAtLink` set path, rdb load, the defrag hash-field path, and hash-field expiry. It adds no test files. I checked `tests/` and `modules/` and found no references to the removed APIs, so nothing in the repo was updated to exercise the new contract. Existing hash and keyspace tests will catch gross breakage, but they don't target the `newItem == 0` NULL-link branch or the `keyFromStoredKey` path directly.

I haven't measured current coverage for these branches, so treat this as a gap to confirm rather than a certain one. A focused dict-level unit test with a dict type that sets `keyFromStoredKey` would cover the conversion contract.
findings.fixPrompt: Add a unit test for the `keyFromStoredKey` contract in the dict code. Use a test dict type whose stored element is a struct with an sds field and set `keyFromStoredKey` to return that sds. Cover `dictAddRaw`, `dictFind`/`dictFindLink`, `dictDelete` and `dictSetKeyAtLink` with both `newItem` values, including the NULL-link branch of `newItem == 0`. Check that lookups by sds find the stored struct, and that delete and rehash keep working. Follow the existing dict unit test style in the repo.

findings.title: __stored_key annotation is a no-op macro with a reserved name
findings.body:
`#define __stored_key` expands to nothing, so the compiler enforces nothing. It only works as a comment in signatures. Identifiers beginning with a double underscore are reserved for the implementation by the C standard, so this name is also technically non-portable. The header comment also says the lookup key and stored key are "the same" when `keyFromStoredKey` is NULL. That's only true because `Entry*` is the field sds (`src/entry.h`), and the header doesn't say so.

Use a plain comment token or a non-reserved name such as `STORED_KEY`, and document the `Entry == field sds` invariant in `dict.h` next to the NULL-callback case.
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/dict.h`, the `#define __stored_key` (around line 66) is a no-op annotation with a reserved identifier name. Rename it to a non-reserved name such as `STORED_KEY` across `dict.h` and `dict.c`, or replace it with a plain comment. Also extend the header comment near that define to state that when `keyFromStoredKey` is NULL, the stored object must be usable directly as the lookup key. For hash dicts this holds because `Entry*` is the field sds, as described in `src/entry.h`.

findings.title: Unrelated changes bundled into the refactor
findings.body:
Several edits don't belong to the stored-key change and make the review harder. `pauseAutoResize` changes from `signed ...:15` to `int16_t`. Its layout should stay the same, but it's a separate concern. There are whitespace-only edits in `dictGenHashFunction` and in the `#define` comment near `activeDefragHfieldDictCallback`. The comment `/* Compiler inlines this for internal calls within dict.c (verified with -O3). */` on `dictGetHash` asserts a build result that a reviewer can't check from the diff. Remove the claim or back it with a reference.

Splitting the pauseAutoResize type change and the whitespace into a separate commit would keep this PR focused.
findings.fixPrompt: Clean up unrelated changes in this PR. In `src/dict.h`, revert the `pauseAutoResize` field type change back to its original bitfield (`signed pauseAutoResize:15`) unless it's needed for this change. In `src/dict.c`, revert the whitespace-only edits in `dictGenHashFunction` and the blank-line edits unrelated to the stored-key change. Remove or substantiate the comment `Compiler inlines this for internal calls within dict.c (verified with -O3)` above `dictGetHash`. Move any remaining cleanup into a separate commit.

findings.title: Hash-field dict paths keep working via Entry/sds identity
findings.body: The hash-field dict types in `src/t_hash.c` (`entryHashDictType`, `entryHashDictTypeWithHFE`) set no `keyFromStoredKey`. `dictStoredKey2Key()` returns the `Entry*` unchanged, which is correct because `entryGetField()` in `src/entry.h` returns the same pointer as the field sds. So removing the old `isSdsField` flag from `hashTypeDelete()` is safe. `onFieldExpire()` already passes `entryGetField(e)`, which is an sds, so its call is correct after the change.

findings.title: Removing the global stored-key toggle is a real safety improvement
findings.body: The old `dictUseStoredKeyApi(d, 1/0)` brackets had to be set and cleared around every call and had to match the dict's type. Missing or misordered brackets would silently hash or compare the wrong representation. This PR removes the flag and all of its call sites in `rdb.c`, `t_hash.c`, `kvstore.c` and `defrag.c`, and the `hashTypeDelete` flag argument goes with them. The lookup/stored distinction now lives in one callback per dict type. I found no remaining references to the removed symbols in `src`, `tests` or `modules`.

findings.title: prefetchValueData now matches the new key-compare contract
findings.body:
`prefetchValueData()` used to pass the `kvobj` to `dictCompareKeys()`. With the stored-key API gone, `keyCompare` takes lookup keys (sds), so passing the sds extracted from the `kvobj` is the correct call. The change is small and matches the new contract.

::diff{file="src/memory_prefetch.c" lines="230-241"}
